paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: The loss comparison between vanilla Transformer and the proposed SepLLM. SepLLM achieves lower loss different computation costs and different training time consistently.
model_annotation: The plot illustrates training loss over time for two model variants, with both curves shown on the same axes to represent how loss changes as training progresses. The x-axis is labeled “Training Time (s)”, uses a linear scale, spans from 0 to 250,000 seconds, and shows regularly spaced tick labels every 50,000 seconds. The y-axis is labeled “Loss”, uses a linear scale, ranges from 2.40 to 2.75, and has tick labels at 0.05 intervals. One line corresponds to “Vanilla” and is drawn in purple with a solid line and upward-pointing triangle markers; it starts near the top of the plotted range (just below 2.75 at early times), decreases to about 2.62 around 50,000 s, continues downward to roughly 2.57 around 100,000 s and about 2.52 around 200,000 s, and ends near 2.50 at 250,000 s. The second line corresponds to “SepLLM” and is drawn in red with a solid line and circular markers; it begins slightly below the purple curve near the upper part of the y-range (around the low 2.7s at early times), declines to about 2.61 around 50,000 s, reaches roughly 2.56 around 100,000 s, approaches about 2.50 near 200,000 s, and ends just under 2.50 (around 2.49) by approximately 230,000–240,000 s. The figure also includes green dashed annotation lines: a horizontal dashed line at loss = 2.50 and two vertical dashed lines near 200,000 s and 250,000 s, with a double-headed arrow between the vertical lines labeled “1.26×”.
